correctness.rationale: For alpha>=2/3, first floor(3alpha)>=2 excludes 1. For 1/2<alpha<2/3, write floor(alpha(2^n+1))=2^(n−1)+floor(2^n(alpha−1/2)+alpha), let N be first positive excess, then 2^(N−1) is unrepresentable. For alpha=2^-k the nonzero floors are binary powers 1,2,4,... and give full coverage. Exact identity H_n=1+alpha(n−3)−sum_{j<=n}{alpha(2^j+1)}+{alpha(2^(n+1)+1)} follows from sum_{j<=n} s_j−s_(n+1)=n−3. If H_n<0, the entire interval (sum floors+1,..., next floor−1) is absent; intervals disjoint. For h!=0, ∫_0^1 |N^-1 sum_{j<=N}exp(2pi i h 2^j alpha)|²dalpha=1/N by orthogonality; Chebyshev and Borel–Cantelli along N=k² plus interpolation imply a.e. Weyl equidistribution, fractional mean 1/2, H_n/n->alpha−1/2. Independently checked 39 exact rational H_n identities. Finite checks do not imply a.e. theorem.
